items.title: PPA Daytona round of 16: Rafael Lenhard comes back from 0-11, Parenteau ends Kelly Goodnow's run, Buckner stops Maria Ford, and four double-digit seeds reach the men's singles quarterfinals
items.summary: Thursday's round of 16 at the Proton Daytona Beach Open set up four men's singles quarterfinals with double-digit seeds in them, per the PPA. No. 10 Rafael Lenhard lost the first game 0-11 to No. 5 Christian Alshon, then won 13-11, 11-6. No. 12 JW Johnson came back from 4-11 down a game to beat No. 7 Noe Khlif in three, and No. 11 Eric Oncins beat No. 6 Roscoe Bellamy 12-10, 11-6. No. 14 Cason Campbell ended No. 26 Mota Alhouni's run, per PickLM's live results. Men's quarterfinals: No. 8 Zane Ford vs. No. 14 Campbell, No. 3 Federico Staksrud vs. No. 12 JW Johnson, No. 2 Hunter Johnson vs. No. 10 Lenhard and No. 4 John Lucian Goins vs. No. 11 Oncins. In women's singles, 14-year-old Kelly Goodnow took the first game 11-9 from defending champion Catherine Parenteau before Parenteau won 11-1, 11-1, and No. 1 Brooke Buckner beat No. 41 Maria Ford after losing the first game, per the PPA and PickLM. No. 11 Sofia Sewing beat No. 7 Cailyn Campbell 11-5, 11-2. Women's quarterfinals: No. 1 Buckner vs. No. 8 Jalina Ingram, No. 3 Judit Castillo vs. No. 5 Isabella Dunlap, No. 2 Kiora Kunimoto vs. No. 11 Sewing and No. 4 Parenteau vs. No. 10 Milan Rane. All doubles quarterfinals are also set, including No. 13 Will Howells/AJ Koller (who beat No. 4 Pablo Tellez/Staksrud) against No. 11 Clayton Powell/Anouar Braham, and Ben Johns/Anna Leigh Waters against Rachel Rohrabacher/Staksrud in mixed, per the PPA and PickLM. Quarterfinals are today on PickleballTV from 12 p.m. ET (11 a.m. CT). Separately, a Pickleball.com staff column on Nov. 19 argued that Genie Bouchard's losses to 13-year-old Natalia Simson and 14-year-old Goodnow raise questions about her commitment to the sport (opinion).

items.title: PPA Daytona round of 32: No. 26 Mota Alhouni knocks out top seed Chris Haworth, Kelly Goodnow beats Genie Bouchard, and No. 41 Maria Ford keeps rolling
items.summary: Wednesday's round of 32 at the Proton Daytona Beach Open, played through rain and wind at Pictona, produced the week's biggest singles upset so far: 26th seed Mota Alhouni beat No. 1 Christopher Haworth 11-4, 11-5, reversing Haworth's 2025 Daytona quarterfinal win over him, per Pickleball.com and the PPA. In women's singles, 14-year-old Kelly Goodnow beat No. 9 seed Genie Bouchard 11-4, 11-3 and plays No. 4 seed and defending champion Catherine Parenteau in today's round of 16. No. 41 Maria Ford, who beat the 13th seed on Tuesday, beat the 15th seed, Helena Jansen, 11-3, 11-9 and now meets No. 1 Brooke Buckner, per the PPA. Anouar Braham reached the round of 16 in all three of his events, clinched in men's doubles with Clayton Powell 11-7, 10-12, 11-3. In women's doubles, 30th seeds Jessica Evanier and Alexa Quintanilla beat the No. 8 seeds, Layne Sleeth and Cailyn Campbell, 11-9, 11-9. John Lucian Goins, chasing a third straight singles title, beat Braden Jacobson 11-6, 11-3. Today's round of 16 brings in the top doubles seeds, including Anna Leigh Waters with Anna Bright and with Ben Johns, with every court on PickleballTV from 12 p.m. ET (11 a.m. CT), per the PPA.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: the creditors' meeting is pushed to Dec. 2, and Pickled! plans to take over the closed Naperville club
items.summary: The Nov. 18 meeting of creditors in The Picklr's Chapter 11 case was adjourned; the docket now sets the 341(a) meeting for Wednesday, Dec. 2 at 3 p.m. by telephone, per a Nov. 18 statement on the court docket. Separately, Chicago-area operator Pickled! says it will take over The Picklr's closed Naperville, Ill. space at 740 Route 59 in Fox River Commons, the Daily Herald/Naperville Sun reported. The Picklr Naperville closed Friday, Nov. 13, per the shopping center's property manager. Pickled! co-owner Nathan Patrick Taylor said there is no opening date yet, that the company is working to reconcile former Picklr members' memberships, and that it may add golf simulators. The Naperville lease rejection is among the motions set for the Dec. 8 hearing.

items.title: USA Pickleball's Collegiate Equipment Program, powered by Selkirk, opens applications Friday, Nov. 20
items.summary: College pickleball clubs can apply for free equipment bundles through USA Pickleball's Collegiate Equipment Program, powered by the Selkirk Growth Program, starting at 12:01 a.m. PT on Friday, Nov. 20 (2:01 a.m. CT), per USA Pickleball. Applicants must be USA Pickleball members in good standing and either current members of a collegiate club or faculty/staff at the school; the club must be listed on USA Pickleball's national collegiate registry. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the window closes once the set number of bundles is awarded, so early applications matter. Equipment must be used by the club, not individual players, and priority goes to clubs with limited equipment, funding or sponsorship.

items.title: Courts watch: Oxford, Miss. accepts a $7.63 million bid for its 24-court Stone Center complex; Scotts Valley keeps its 8 p.m. closing while it surveys
items.summary: Oxford's Board of Aldermen on Tuesday, Nov. 17 accepted Wagner General Contractors' low bid of $7,632,240, including all four alternates, for the Stone Center pickleball complex: 18 covered courts, six outdoor courts, two parking lots and a raised platform, per the meeting record. The bid came in about $1.4 million under the low end of the architect's $9 million estimate, Oxford News Now reported, and the 420-day schedule points to a January 2028 opening. In Scotts Valley, Calif., the City Council discussed noise and traffic complaints about the Skypark courts on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and took no action. The 8 p.m. nightly closing from the summer pilot stays in place while the city surveys residents and court users through Nov. 30; results go to the Parks and Recreation Commission on Dec. 17, per SFGate/Bay City News and the city.

items.title: USA Pickleball and JOOLA end their legal fight and team up, with JOOLA giving $150,000 a year in equipment to USA Pickleball Serves
items.summary: USA Pickleball and JOOLA announced a strategic partnership on Tuesday, Nov. 17, which USA Pickleball says follows the resolution of litigation between the two organizations; no settlement terms were announced. JOOLA becomes an official sponsor of USA Pickleball Serves, the governing body's charitable arm, and will contribute $150,000 in equipment each year for programs serving youth and schools, service members and first responders, adaptive pickleball, and grant programs such as Grow the Game and Play It Forward. The deal also covers USA Pickleball's national events, player development and coach education, per the announcement. Separately, USA Pickleball said it will expand coaching resources through RacketPro Organization (RPO) and work with 150+ Health on programming for older adults.

items.title: MLP names Tanner Groff its new commissioner, moving over from running events for the PPA Tour
items.summary: Major League Pickleball named Tanner Groff its commissioner on Monday, Nov. 16, per the league. Groff, most recently Pickleball Inc.'s senior vice president of events, helped build the PPA Challenger Series (more than 30 events a year) and the Powerball Amateur State Championship Series. As commissioner he runs all MLP league operations, with a focus on owner relations and on-court competition. Chief tour officer Zach Gallin takes over MLP event operations, production, fan experience and financials, and Courtney Johnson was promoted to senior director of team competition for MLP and senior director of officiating for the PPA. Former commissioner Samin Odhwani stays on as a strategic advisor, per pickleball.com. MLP says more 2027 season information is coming in the next few weeks.

items.title: Brisbane 2032 organizers say pickleball won't be considered for the Olympics because the sport has no recognized international federation
items.summary: The Brisbane 2032 organizing committee told ABC News (Australia) that pickleball will not be considered for the 2032 Olympic program because it doesn't meet the criteria, including having a recognized international federation. The same ABC profile reported that committee president Andrew Liveris holds an interest in almost 70% of the equity in the holding company behind PPA Tour Australia, whose president is his son Anthony; Liveris declared a potential conflict in 2024 and declined to answer the ABC's questions about pickleball. The IOC only adds sports governed by IOC-recognized federations, and no pickleball body has that recognition yet, per World Pickleball Magazine and The Kitchen. The Kitchen notes the IOC's final vote on the Brisbane program is set for April 2027.

items.title: APP Arizona Open: 41st seed Alvi Regalado wins men's singles in his first APP event, Kat Stewart takes women's singles 11-4, 11-0

Millet leaves with doubles gold and singles silver. Kat Stewart beat Domenika Turkovic 11-4, 11-0 for her fifth women's pro singles gold of the season, per the APP; Turkovic had won the APP's previous two women's singles titles, per World Pickleball Magazine. Turkovic still won gold: she and Jay Devilliers, the No. 12 seeds, beat No. 6 seeds Vivian Glozman and Ronan Camron 11-2, 11-9 in the mixed final. Bronzes went to Max Green (over Ryler DeHeart 1-11, 11-9, 11-9), Roos Van Reek (over Amanda Hendry 11-0, 12-10) and, in mixed, Megan Fudge and Aidan Schenk, per the APP. Fudge's bronze isn't a gold, so her APP record of 33 women's pro golds stays shared with Simone Jardim.

items.summary: Patrick Kawka and Andre Millet beat Jack Munro and Richard Livornese Jr. 3-11, 11-3, 11-5 to win men's pro doubles at the APP Arizona Open in Mesa on Saturday, per the APP Tour. Munro and Livornese came in with seven straight APP men's doubles titles this season, per World Pickleball Magazine. Tanner Tomassi and Jay Devilliers took bronze 11-2, 11-8. In women's pro doubles, Vivian Glozman and Roos Van Reek beat Kat Stewart and Brooke Revuelta 11-6, 11-8 for the title, and Arielle Butler and Allison Harris took bronze 1-11, 11-2, 11-9, per the APP. Megan Fudge, who came to Mesa level with Simone Jardim on a record 33 women's pro golds (per WPM), won't get a 34th gold in Mesa: she and Aidan Schenk lost the mixed semifinal, and she and Jada Bui missed the women's doubles podium, so the record stays shared. Millet is also in Sunday's men's singles final against 41st seed Alvi Regalado; Stewart plays Domenika Turkovic for the women's singles title. Championship Sunday streams on ESPN+, with bronze matches from 11 a.m. ET, per the APP.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy reaches the clubs: Newark, Del. closes abruptly, Denton, Texas shut in October, and more lease motions hit the docket
items.summary: The Picklr's 12-court club at The Grove in Newark, Del. closed abruptly this week, just over a year after it opened, per the Newark Post; Delaware Online also reported the closure. The Newark Post says founder and CEO Jorge Barragan told Sports Business Journal that some of the company's problems trace back to guaranteeing lease payments for about 40 franchisees. In Texas, the Denton club closed for good on Oct. 16 after its landlord ended the lease based on the bankruptcy filing, said Murko Group, the franchise group that opened it; many members moved to its McKinney and Lewisville clubs, per Community Impact. In court, the debtors filed another motion to reject a lease on Nov. 13 (Dkt. 122) and on Nov. 14 filed a notice of hearing (Dkt. 124) covering the Naperville, Ill. lease rejection (Dkt. 109) and procedures to pay professionals (Dkt. 121), per the Omni docket. That follows the final DIP order signed Nov. 13.

items.title: Study: pickleball arm and shoulder injuries skew toward women and players over 60, and fractures are the most common
items.summary: A descriptive study reported by Healio estimated 14,916 pickleball-related upper-extremity injuries in U.S. emergency-department data from 2014 to 2023. Players over 60 accounted for 83.1% and women for 59%. Fractures were the most common injury (58.6%, versus 36.1% of comparable tennis injuries), and the shoulder (36.4%) and forearm (34%) were the most-injured areas. Injury incidence per 100,000 players peaked in 2021 at 62.74, versus 5.27 in 2015 and 30.6 in 2022.

items.title: Gear: USA Pickleball delists the CPX Hyper+ elongated 14mm and 16mm paddles after retail samples failed compliance testing
items.summary: USA Pickleball has removed the CPX Hyper+ elongated 14mm and 16mm models from its certified paddle list after courtside testing and market sampling found significant differences in PBCoR and deflection between the paddles submitted for certification and mass-production units sold to players. USA Pickleball's Nov. 2 equipment statement says it is working with CPX on new versions under a new model name. CPX's own Hyper+ update page says some recent production units played hotter than the certified samples, that current Hyper+ paddles are not for USA Pickleball-sanctioned events, and that a Hyper+ 2 is in recertification with dual factory/warehouse testing and serial numbers planned. The Dink, reporting Nov. 5 from the USA Pickleball Nationals in San Diego, says officials told paddle reviewer John Kew that potential financial penalties against CPX are 'in consideration.' No fines have been announced. Rec play is unaffected; tournament players who need an approved paddle can request a Hyper+ 2 swap once it is available, per CPX.
